I have been doing this same wheat-maize for twenty years. I do what my neighbors do. What worked last year, I do again this year. Change is risky, and my husband works in town some days so I must decide many things by myself.

For my wheat in autumn — I plant improved seed. The seed shop in the village sells the same kind everyone here uses, my neighbor Liu Sao got 500 jin per mu last year so I buy what she buys. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind in the big white bags. I use about two bags per mu as base, that is 100 jin, 50 kg. Then in spring when wheat turns green I topdress urea, one bag for every two mu, so about 25 jin per mu. If the wheat looks yellow I add a little more — better to spend a few extra yuan than lose the harvest. My well water, I irrigate before winter once so roots don't freeze, then at greening, then at jointing, then at filling if it is dry. Four times usually. Spray twice — once for yellow rust and aphids together in spring, once later if I see more bugs.

For maize in summer — right after wheat harvest my cousin comes with the seeder. Hybrid seed only, the Zhengdan kind, everyone uses it. I put compound fertilizer down when sowing, one and a half bags per mu, then side-dress urea at knee-high stage, maybe 30 jin per mu. Maize drinks a lot of water in July-August so I irrigate two-three times from the well. One spray for armyworm and borer is usually enough, sometimes two if the pests are bad.

I don't plough deep anymore, the machine man just does rotary — cheaper, faster. Plough costs more and my field is not hard.

My costs must balance. Fertilizer takes most of my money. I don't skip it because without fertilizer there is no grain.
